chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from more than one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning two men who had two dirhams with them: one of them said, "The two dirhams are mine," and the other said, "They are between me and you." So he said, "As for the one who said, 'They are between me and you,' he has admitted that one of the two dirhams is not his and that it belongs to his companion; and the other is to be divided between them."

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: admitted or acknowledged, establishing a legal concession
key_terms.بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ: shared between me and you, indicating partial acknowledgment of another's claim
key_terms.دِرْهَمَانِ: two dirhams, the disputed property in this case
key_terms.لِصَاحِبِهِ: belonging to his companion, affirming the other party's ownership
key_terms.يُقْسَمُ: is divided, referring to apportionment of the remaining disputed amount

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rule when two people dispute ownership of two dirhams and one admits partial sharing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a dispute over shared property when one claimant partially acknowledges the other's right. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the admission establishes ownership of one dirham for the other party, while the remaining dirham is divided equally between them. It reflects principles of acknowledgment, evidence through admission, and fair division in financial disputes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3274 - In the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (as):

Two men had two dirhams with them.
One of them said: "Both dirhams are mine."
The other said: "They are shared between me and you."
Imam (as) said: "As for the one who said: 'They are shared between me and you,' he has admitted that one of the dirhams does not belong to him and is his companion's.
The remaining dirham should be divided equally between them."
